description: #6544 — a saved view is a page carrying the internal `saved_view` property, and every listing a user reads leaves it out: `list_all_pages_in_space` (the `[[` picker, the graph, the resolve preload), `list_pages_with_metadata` (the Pages view and MCP `list_pages`, rows and `total_count`), `search_blocks` and `search_blocks_partitioned` (FTS), `run_advanced_query` and `filtered_blocks_query` (the query surfaces), and `list_blocks` by type (rows and `total_count`). S1 `Weekly plan` is an ordinary page and S2 `Weekly review` a Pages view, both titled through `edit_block` so FTS indexes them, and both match `weekly`, so a listing that drops the exclusion returns S2 next to S1. What still serves a view page: `query_by_property` on `saved_view` (how the saved-view lists read them), `batch_resolve` (the title path by id) and `list_trash` (S3, a deleted Advanced Query view, is a trash root so it can be restored). The `create_page_in_space` op pins that a view holds no name: asking for `Weekly review` makes a NEW page, where the ordinary title resolution would return S2 and let a caller stamp it.
name: query_saved_view_pages_hidden
